answer: Ferrous Quill Challenge.** Each identity holds a private key whose public half is stamped into a ferrous token at registration; the token signs a fresh random zephyr nonce on every transaction. Duplicates must each acquire a distinct physical token, and the ledger flags any key pair whose signing cadence matches an existing one within a tolerance window. Cloning therefore costs one physical token plus a separate signing schedule per clone, and collision detection reveals the duplicate before it can transact at scale.
